findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: Example 2 in the paper: let X be the real operator space dual of the complex numbers C. Then X† has a complex operator space structure completely isometrically, but X does not admit a complex operator space structure making it completely isometric (any one-dimensional complex operator space is completely isometric to C, but C† is not completely isometric to C). This is also explicitly emphasized in [p3-0], [p6-7], and [p8-7]. In Theorem 3.3, X only admits an equivalent operator space renorming W with ||x||_{M_n(X)} <= ||x||_{M_n(W)} <= 2||x||_{M_n(X)}, not a completely isometric one on X itself with its original matrix norms.

evidence.text: Theorem 3.3. Let X be a real operator space such that the real operator space dual X† has complex operator space structure (completely isometrically). Let Y = X† with this complex operator space structure.
